title: story-062 live-staker pause has no break-glass: a mid-suite halt strands the LIVE original staker (and the unrelated un-migrated USDe pool) paused; unpause reachable only via a fully-successful PostMigrationCleanup
sourceContract: lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol (whenNotPaused on stake/withdraw; pause is contract-global)
entryPointNote: Side-effect spans migrate:ys-swap-deploy (sets pause) and migrate:ys-swap-cleanup (the only unpause path). Primary fingerprint entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-deploy.
description: story-062 deploy now calls setPauser(OWNER)+pause() on BOTH stakers, including the LIVE original. Pause is contract-global, so it also freezes the un-migrated USDe pool for the whole window. The ONLY code that unpauses + restores the original staker's pauser is PostMigrationCleanup (unpause at ~329, setPauser restore at ~342). But cleanup hard-requires ~12 verifications + the solvency invariant (lines 174-304) to pass BEFORE it reaches the unpause; a migration that is incomplete or insolvent cannot reach the unpause. There is no standalone 'unpause/restore' script in script/. So a suite that halts after deploy (e.g. the leg1 withdrawer revert 106d5c6e, or the YS-04 gather off-by-one preflight DoS, or any mid-suite mainnet halt — the exact scenario story-062 was hardening for) leaves the live original staker paused (all stake/withdraw frozen for DOLA, USDC AND the untouched USDe pool) until the operator either completes the entire migration or manually unpauses out-of-band.
impact: Real user-facing DoS on the LIVE original staker — all stake/withdraw frozen for DOLA, USDC AND the unrelated, un-migrated USDe pool — for the entire duration of any mid-suite halt. Pause is contract-global. The only unpause path (PostMigrationCleanup ~329 + pauser-restore ~342) is gated behind ~12 verifications + the solvency invariant, so an incomplete/insolvent migration cannot reach it; there is no standalone reopen script in script/. Recovery is coupled to full-migration success rather than an independent break-glass, so on failure the freeze window is unbounded by code. Assets are not at direct risk (frozen, not lost; owner-recoverable via manual setPauser/unpause out-of-band).
attackPath: 1. deploy calls setPauser(OWNER)+pause() on both stakers, including the LIVE original (contract-global pause; freezes USDe pool too).
2. Suite halts mid-way (e.g. the 106d5c6e leg1 withdrawer revert, or any mid-suite mainnet condition — exactly what story-062 was hardening for).
3. Cleanup's unpause is unreachable because the full verify+solvency gate cannot pass on an incomplete migration; no break-glass script exists.
4. Live staker + USDe users remain frozen until the operator completes the entire migration or manually unpauses out-of-band.
forkEvidence: fork: after deploy broadcast, original staker 0xbce8..079A paused()==true, pauser==OWNER. After full cleanup, paused()==false, pauser restored to 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3. No script/*.s.sol other than PostMigrationCleanup calls unpause() (confirmed by directory scan). cleanup's unpause is downstream of the full verify+solvency gate.
recommendation: Ship a minimal standalone 'EmergencyUnpauseAndRestorePausers' script (reads origPauser/tempPauser from ys-swap-deployments.json, unpauses, restores) that the operator can run if the suite halts, decoupled from the migration-complete verifications. Document the live-pool freeze (esp. the unrelated USDe pool) and its expected duration in the runbook.
relatedFindings: 55ebe2c0 (FIXED YS-09 — the story-062 hardening that INTRODUCED this pause side-effect; MUST NOT be netted against the YS-09 fix)
doNotNet: Distinct from FIXED YS-09 (55ebe2c0). The story-062 fix that earned YS-09 its FIXED verdict INTRODUCED this pause-DoS surface. Both stand; do not collapse.
